business_problem: Wolt needed a scalable way to understand merchant density, delivery coverage, and expansion opportunities across hundreds of cities without relying on ad hoc geospatial analysis that could not keep up with its 27-country marketplace.
solution_summary: Wolt built a geospatial analytics stack on Snowflake to model delivery coverage and expansion opportunities across its marketplace. Merchant delivery radii and city datasets are loaded into Snowflake, then combined with Wolt's proprietary H3-based geospatial index and a population dataset with more than 2 million rows. Using Snowflake's native geospatial support and SQL functions for H3, the team fills coverage polygons with hex cells, joins them to population data, and calculates catchment, density, and coverage gaps down to 200-meter resolution. Market managers, sales leaders, and expansion teams use the resulting views to compare candidate markets, identify underserved neighborhoods, and prioritize density-first growth. By moving from an ad hoc proof of concept to a repeatable Snowflake workflow, Wolt reduced the time required to wrangle data for intra-country expansion decisions by 80% and gave local and international teams a consistent view of hyperlocal market opportunity.

solution_components.name: Snowflake
solution_components.role: Hosts Wolt's geospatial datasets and executes the joins and coverage calculations needed for market analysis at scale.

solution_components.name: H3
solution_components.role: Provides the hexagonal geospatial index Wolt uses to standardize coverage and population analysis across countries and cities.

data_flow: Merchant radii, Wolt city datasets, and global population data are loaded into Snowflake, where H3-based geospatial joins convert coverage polygons into comparable hex-cell analytics. The resulting coverage, density, and gap views are consumed by market managers, sales leaders, and expansion teams for local and international growth decisions.
business_outcome: Wolt cut data wrangling for expansion decisions by 80%, gave local and global teams a repeatable way to compare candidate markets, and improved customer experience by identifying underserved areas and building merchant density before scaling outward.
metrics: 80% less time required to wrangle data for intra-country expansion decisions
